claims.title: Inference requests may be readable on the public path to the gateway
claims.description: `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `boundary:serving-edge` and carries inference requests including end-user text, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If transport encryption is not enabled, an on-path observer between `entity:calling-service` and the internet-facing `process:inference-gateway` can intercept the requests and read their PII. The disclosed prompts can reveal customer-user content and provide inputs an attacker could reuse when targeting the inference service.

quotes.text: Callers pass an API key in a header.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request` crosses a public-to-serving boundary, but `encryption_in_transit` is unverified. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `pii` and carries end-user inference text.

mitigations.summary: Require TLS for public inference submission
mitigations.detail: Set verified TLS 1.2+ for `flow:entity:calling-service>process:inference-gateway>submit-inference-request`; require callers to validate the gateway certificate.

claims.title: Requests forwarded into the model network may be readable between the gateway and model server
claims.description: `flow:process:inference-gateway>process:model-server>forward-request` crosses from `boundary:serving-edge` into `boundary:model-network`, carries an inference-request payload, and has `encryption_in_transit` unknown. If the internal hop is unencrypted, an attacker able to observe that boundary-crossing path can intercept PII-bearing requests before `process:model-server` uses them. The captured request content can expose customer inputs and aid targeted attacks against the model-serving path.

quotes.text: The gateway forwards the request to the model server

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses the serving-edge-to-model-network boundary while `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `pii` and carries inference request payloads.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the gateway-to-model-server hop
mitigations.detail: Use TLS or mTLS on `flow:process:inference-gateway>process:model-server>forward-request` and verify both service identities.

claims.title: Model artifacts may be readable while the model server loads them
claims.description: `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact` transfers a model artifact from `store:model-registry-bucket` to `process:model-server`, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If this object-storage connection lacks transport protection, an observer with a foothold on the model-network path can intercept the artifact. A copied artifact can expose proprietary model behavior and help an attacker study the serving model offline.

quotes.text: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `encryption_in_transit` is unknown and an attacker must first obtain visibility on the internal model-network path. Impact is low because the model identifies the transferred asset only as `business-critical-data`, without stating that it contains customer records, credentials, or secrets.

mitigations.detail: Require TLS for `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact` and configure the model server to validate the storage endpoint certificate.

claims.title: Customer feature reads may be readable on the model-network connection
claims.description: `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` carries per-customer account-age and spend-band data and has `encryption_in_transit` unknown. If Redis transport protection is absent, an observer on the model-network connection can intercept these reads and recover PII and financial attributes. The captured attributes can be correlated with inference requests forwarded to `process:model-server` to profile customers more completely.

quotes.text: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` has unverified transport protection and an attacker needs an internal path position. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is classified confidential and tagged `pii` and `financial`.

mitigations.detail: Use TLS for `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features`, validate the Redis endpoint identity, and restrict network access to the named model-server workload.

claims.title: Raw prompts and responses may be readable while being written to the inference log
claims.description: `flow:process:inference-gateway>store:inference-log>write-request-log` sends raw prompts and model responses to `store:inference-log`, but `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If that BigQuery API path is not transport-protected, an observer able to access the serving-edge path can intercept the debugging records. The disclosure persists beyond an individual request because the intercepted content is also material that `store:inference-log` retains for debugging.

quotes.text: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging.
That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the write path remains within the serving-edge zone and `encryption_in_transit` is unknown, so an attacker needs path visibility. Impact is medium because `store:inference-log` is tagged `pii` and records raw user prompts and responses.

mitigations.detail: Verify TLS for `flow:process:inference-gateway>store:inference-log>write-request-log`, including certificate validation by the gateway.
Redact or tokenize personal data in prompts and responses before they are sent to `store:inference-log`.

claims.title: Model artifacts may be readable while engineers publish them to the registry
claims.description: `flow:entity:ml-engineer>store:model-registry-bucket>publish-artifact` transfers model artifacts to `store:model-registry-bucket`, but its `encryption_in_transit` is unknown. If encryption is absent, an on-path observer of the engineer-to-registry connection can intercept a newly published model artifact. The copy may reveal proprietary model implementation and can be analyzed before it is loaded by `process:model-server`.

quotes.text: ML engineers publish new model artifacts to the registry bucket.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because `encryption_in_transit` is unknown and interception requires access to the engineer-to-registry path. Impact is low because the model identifies the artifact as `business-critical-data` but does not state that it holds customer data, credentials, or secrets.

mitigations.detail: Require encrypted object-storage API transport and endpoint certificate validation on `flow:entity:ml-engineer>store:model-registry-bucket>publish-artifact`.

claims.title: A copied model-registry volume may disclose model artifacts if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:model-registry-bucket` holds model artifacts and its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to no effective encryption at rest, an attacker who obtains an operational copy such as exported media, a snapshot, or a backup can read stored artifacts without using `process:model-server`'s service account. The copied artifacts can be studied offline to reveal proprietary model behavior and implementation details. This is conditional on the unresolved at-rest protection state, not an assertion that the bucket is unencrypted.

quotes.text: The model server loads model artifacts from a model registry bucket at startup.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:model-registry-bucket` has unverified at-rest encryption and operational copies can be obtained without live application access if protection is absent. Impact is low because the bucket's data classification is unknown and its stated asset is `business-critical-data`.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption for the registry and its copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the `encryption_at_rest` posture for `store:model-registry-bucket`; require managed encryption keys for the bucket, backups, snapshots, and exports, and limit export access.

claims.title: A copied Redis volume may disclose confidential customer financial features
claims.description: `store:redis-feature-store` is classified confidential, contains PII and financial customer features, and has `encryption_at_rest` unknown. If storage encryption is absent, an attacker holding a disk image, backup, snapshot, or other operational copy can read account-age and spend-band records without authenticating through the live Redis service. Those records can be correlated with requests processed by `process:model-server` to profile affected customers. This draft is conditional on the unresolved `encryption_at_rest` attribute.

quotes.text: The features include account age and spend bands per customer.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:redis-feature-store` has unverified at-rest encryption and storage copies bypass live Redis access controls if encryption is absent. Impact is high because the store is classified confidential and tagged `pii` and `financial`.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt Redis data and operational copies at rest
mitigations.detail: Verify then enforce encryption at rest for `store:redis-feature-store`, including backups, snapshots, and replicas, with keys restricted to the minimum storage-administration principals.

mitigations.summary: Reduce the sensitivity of stored features
mitigations.detail: Tokenize customer identifiers and apply field-level protection to the highest-sensitivity financial attributes where Redis access patterns permit it.

claims.title: A copied inference-log dataset may disclose retained raw user prompts
claims.description: `store:inference-log` retains every request and response, including raw prompts, and its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If the BigQuery data and its operational copies are not effectively encrypted at rest, an attacker who obtains an export, backup, or storage-layer copy can read retained prompts without calling `process:inference-gateway`. Because prompts may contain whatever end users typed, the copied dataset can disclose PII at a scale larger than one intercepted request. This is conditional on the unverified at-rest encryption state.

quotes.text: The gateway writes every request and response into an inference log in BigQuery, for debugging.
That means raw prompts, which sometimes carry whatever the calling team's users typed.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:inference-log` has unverified at-rest encryption and an exported or copied dataset bypasses the gateway. Impact is medium because the store is tagged `pii` and retains raw user-entered prompts and model responses.

mitigations.summary: Protect inference-log storage and exports with encryption
mitigations.detail: Verify `store:inference-log` encryption at rest, require it for all exports and backups, and restrict data-extract permissions to approved logging administrators.

mitigations.summary: Apply retention and redaction to debug records
mitigations.detail: Redact sensitive prompt fields before logging and retain raw request and response content only for the shortest operationally necessary period.

claims.title: An internal attacker may read all Redis customer features if no authentication beyond the absent password exists
claims.description: `store:redis-feature-store` contains confidential PII and financial features, and `flow:process:model-server>store:redis-feature-store>read-features` has authentication recorded as unknown. The source specifically states that Redis has no password, although that does not settle whether another authentication mechanism exists. If no compensating Redis authentication is configured, an attacker with access to the model network can connect to the store and read customer account-age and spend-band records directly. The disclosure can then be correlated with inference activity handled by `process:model-server`; this draft is conditional on the unresolved authentication mechanism beyond the absent password.

quotes.text: Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the store is stated to be internal, so an attacker needs a model-network foothold, but the source states that Redis has no password and the remaining authentication is unknown. Impact is high because `store:redis-feature-store` is confidential and tagged `pii` and `financial`.

mitigations.detail: Configure Redis authentication and authorization for `store:redis-feature-store`, use a distinct credential or workload identity for `process:model-server`, and deny unauthenticated connections.

mitigations.summary: Limit network access to the feature store
mitigations.detail: Enforce network policy so only the named model-server workload can reach the Redis endpoint, rather than treating model-network presence as authorization.

claims.title: Code executing in the model server can read registry artifacts through its service account
claims.description: `process:model-server` reads `store:model-registry-bucket` through `flow:process:model-server>store:model-registry-bucket>load-artifact` using its own service account. An attacker who obtains code execution in `process:model-server` can use that established read path to copy registry artifacts without needing to compromise an ML engineer account. The copied artifact can be analyzed offline to disclose proprietary model behavior; the documented service-account read path should therefore be scoped to only the required artifact objects and versions.

quotes.text: It uses its own service account for that.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because the attacker must first obtain code execution in `process:model-server`; no such initial compromise is stated. Impact is low because `store:model-registry-bucket` is identified only with `business-critical-data`, while its data classification is unknown.

mitigations.summary: Scope the model-server identity to required artifacts
mitigations.detail: Restrict the service account used by `process:model-server` to read only the approved model object prefixes and versions needed at startup.

mitigations.summary: Use short-lived workload credentials and audit artifact reads
mitigations.detail: Issue short-lived workload identity tokens for registry access and alert on artifact reads inconsistent with normal model-server startup behavior.
